questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन भारतीय पुरातत्त्व सर्वेक्षण (A.S.I.) के पहले महानिदेशक थे ?
questions.text_english: Who among the following was the first Director General of Archaeological Survey of India (A.S.I.) ?
questions.solution: Alexander Cunningham was the first Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India. He is often known as the father of Indian archaeology, having laid the foundation for systematic archaeological research in the 19th century.

questions.text: स्तंभ-I का मिलान स्तंभ-II से कीजिए और निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Match Column-I with Column-II and choose the correct option from the following:
questions.solution: The correct matches are: Manda in Jammu, Rakhigarhi in Haryana, Nageshwar in Gujarat, and Kalibangan in Rajasthan. Therefore, option A is the correct sequence.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित घटनाओं को कालक्रमिक क्रम से व्यवस्थित कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए:
questions.text_english: Arrange the following events in a chronological order and choose the correct option:
questions.instruction_line: I. गुप्त शासन की शुरुआत, II. मौर्य साम्राज्य का अंत, III. तमिलनाडु में पल्लवों का उदय, IV. कन्नौज के राजा के रूप में हर्षवर्धन का उदय
questions.instruction_line_english: I. Beginning of Gupta rule, II. End of Mauryan Empire, III. Rise of Pallavas in Tamil Nadu, IV. Rise of Harshavardhana as a king of Kannauj
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is: End of Mauryan Empire (c. 2nd century BCE), Beginning of Gupta rule (c. 320 CE), Rise of Pallavas (c. 6th century CE), and Rise of Harshavardhana (c. 7th century CE). Thus, option B is correct.

questions.text: दिए गए विकल्पों में से प्राचीन मंदिर के इस चित्र की पहचान कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Identify the given image of ancient temple from the given options:
questions.solution: The image depicts the Kailashnath temple at Ellora, which is a monolithic structure carved from a single massive rock, famous for its architectural brilliance during the Rashtrakuta period.

questions.text: बुद्ध का पहला उपदेश _______ में दिया गया था।
questions.text_english: The first Sermon of the Buddha was delivered at _______.
questions.solution: Buddha gave his first sermon at Sarnath, near Varanasi, after attaining enlightenment at Bodh Gaya. This event is historically known as 'Dharmachakra Pravartana' or the turning of the wheel of law.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित जानकारी की सहायता से महाभारत के पात्र की पहचान कीजिए : वह भीम का पुत्र था। वह मातृ पक्ष से राक्षस वंश से था ।
questions.text_english: Identify the character of Mahabharata with the help of following information: He was the son of Bheema. He belonged to Rakshasa clan from maternal side.
questions.solution: Ghatotkacha was the son of Bheema and the demoness Hidimba. He belonged to the Rakshasa clan through his mother, and he fought heroically in the Mahabharata war on the side of the Pandavas.

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : आरंभिक भारतीय इतिहास में छठी शताब्दी ई.पू. को एक महत्त्वपूर्ण परिवर्तनकारी काल माना जाता है। कारण (R) : इस काल को आरंभिक राज्यों, नगरों, लोहे के बढ़ते प्रयोग, सिक्कों के विकास एवं बुद्ध धर्म तथा जैन धर्म के विकास के साथ जोड़ा जाता है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): The sixth century BCE is often regarded as a major turning point in early Indian history. Reason (R) : This was an era associated with early states, cities, use of iron, development of coinage and growth of Buddhism and Jainism.
questions.instruction_line: विकल्प: (A) (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है। (B) (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। (C) (A) सही है, परन्तु (R) गलत है। (D) (A) गलत है, परन्तु (R) सही है।
questions.instruction_line_english: Options: (A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). (B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A). (C) (A) is true but (R) is untrue. (D) (A) is not true but (R) is true.

options.A: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं और (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: (A) और (R) दोनों सही हैं परन्तु (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।

options_english.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.B: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
options_english.D: (A) is not true but (R) is true.

questions.solution: The 6th century BCE was indeed a turning point as it witnessed the rise of Mahajanapadas, urban growth, and the rise of heterodox sects like Buddhism and Jainism, which is correctly linked to the developments mentioned in the Reason.

questions.text: नीचे दी गई जानकारी की सहायता से प्रारंभिक भक्ति परंपरा की स्त्री भक्त के नाम की पहचान कीजिए : वह शिव भक्त थीं । उन्होंने अपने उद्देश्य प्राप्ति हेतु घोर तपस्या का मार्ग अपनाया ।
questions.text_english: Identify the name of a woman devotee of early Bhakti tradition with the help of information given below : She was a devotee of Lord Shiva. She adopted a path of extreme asceticism to attain her goal.
questions.solution: Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a devotee of Lord Shiva and famously adopted a path of severe asceticism to attain spiritual goals. She is one of the earliest known Nayanars in the Bhakti tradition.

questions.text: विजयनगर साम्राज्य के समकालीन राज्यों के संदर्भ में कौन सा विकल्प सही नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following option is NOT correct regarding the contemporaries of Vijayanagara empire?

options.A: उड़ीसा के गजपति राज्य की स्थापना

options_english.A: Establishment of the Gajapati Kingdom of Orissa
options_english.B: Establishment of the Sultanates of Malwa
options_english.D: Rise of the Chalukyas in Karnataka

questions.solution: The Chalukyas of Karnataka belonged to an earlier period (roughly 6th-12th century CE) and were not contemporaries of the Vijayanagara Empire, which was established in the 14th century.

questions.text: विजयनगर साम्राज्य के संबंध में निम्नलिखित विकल्पों में से सही कथन का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Choose the correct statement from the following options with reference to Vijayanagara empire:

options.A: इस साम्राज्य की स्थापना सुलुव वंश द्वारा की गई।
options.B: कृष्णदेव राय की मृत्यु के पश्चात यह साम्राज्य शक्तिशाली हो गया ।
options.C: तालीकोटा का युद्ध इस साम्राज्य के लिए विनाशकारी साबित हुआ ।
options.D: इनकी भू-राजस्व प्रणाली मनसबदारी प्रणाली से ली गई थी।

options_english.A: This empire was founded by the rulers of Saluva dynasty.
options_english.B: This empire became powerful after the death of Krishnadeva Raya.
options_english.C: The battle of Talikota proved disastrous for Vijayanagara empire.
options_english.D: Their land revenue system was taken from Mansabdari system.

questions.solution: The Battle of Talikota (1565) was a major defeat for the Vijayanagara Empire, which led to the sacking of the capital city and marked the beginning of its decline. The other statements are factually incorrect.

questions.text: विजयनगर साम्राज्य के संदर्भ में स्तंभ-1 का मिलान स्तंभ-II से कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Match Column-I with Column-II regarding Vijayanagara empire and choose the correct option:
questions.instruction_line: Column I: Nicolo de Conti, Abdur Razzak, Duarte Barbosa, Afanasi Nikitin. Column II: Persia, Portugal, Italy, Russia.
questions.instruction_line_english: Column I: Nicolo de Conti, Abdur Razzak, Duarte Barbosa, Afanasi Nikitin. Column II: Persia, Portugal, Italy, Russia.
questions.solution: Nicolo de Conti was from Italy, Abdur Razzak from Persia, Duarte Barbosa from Portugal, and Afanasi Nikitin from Russia. Matching these gives sequence A.

questions.text: मुगल राज्य में कृषि के निरंतर विस्तार में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा एक प्रमुख कारक नहीं था ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following was not a major factor that accounted for the constant expansion of agriculture in the Mughal state?
questions.solution: The availability of tractors is a modern agricultural phenomenon and not a historical factor from the Mughal period. Factors like abundant land, labour, and mobile peasants contributed to agricultural growth then.

questions.text: मुगलों की भू-राजस्व प्रणाली के संदर्भ में स्तंभ-I का मिलान स्तंभ-II के साथ कीजिए :
questions.text_english: With reference to the land revenue system of the Mughals, match Column-I with that of Column-II:
questions.instruction_line: Column I: Jama, Khet Batai, Lang Batai, Hasil. Column II: The amount of revenue assessed, Field divided after sowing, Crops divided after harvesting, Actually collected amount.
questions.instruction_line_english: Column I: Jama, Khet Batai, Lang Batai, Hasil. Column II: The amount of revenue assessed, Field divided after sowing, Crops divided after harvesting, Actually collected amount.
questions.solution: In Mughal land revenue, 'Jama' was the assessed amount, 'Khet Batai' was dividing the field after sowing, 'Lang Batai' was dividing heaps of crops after harvest, and 'Hasil' was the amount actually collected. Option A reflects this correctly.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा जोड़ा सुमेलित है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched ?
questions.instruction_line: Sufi teacher and their Dargah location.
questions.instruction_line_english: Sufi teacher and their Dargah location.
questions.solution: Shaikh Nizamuddin Auliya's Dargah is located in Delhi. The others are incorrectly matched (Moinuddin Chishti is in Ajmer, Kaki in Delhi, and Ganj-i-Shakar in Ajodhan).

questions.text: 1770 में निम्नलिखित में से किसने भागलपुर में पहाड़ियों के साथ 'शांति की नीति' का प्रस्ताव दिया ?
questions.text_english: Who among the following proposed a Policy of Pacification' with the Paharias in 1770 in Bhagalpur?
questions.solution: Augustus Cleveland, the Collector of Bhagalpur, proposed the 'Policy of Pacification' in 1770s to bring the Paharia people into the mainstream and maintain order in the region.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित को कालानुक्रमिक क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए और सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Arrange the following in chronological order and choose the correct option.
questions.instruction_line: I. अंग्रेजों द्वारा पारित परिसीमन कानून, II. बंगाल में इस्तमरारी बंदोबस्त का प्रारंभ, III. संथाल विद्रोह, IV. बॉम्बे दक्कन में रैयतवारी प्रणाली
questions.instruction_line_english: I. Limitation Law passed by the British, II. Starting of Permanent Settlement in Bengal, III. Santhal Rebellion, IV. Ryotwari settlement in Bombay Deccan
questions.solution: Chronology: Permanent Settlement (1793), Ryotwari in Bombay Deccan (1820s), Santhal Rebellion (1855), and Limitation Law (1859). Option C follows this correct timeline.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित विकल्पों में से संविधान सभा के संबंध में 26 नवंबर, 1949 के महत्त्व का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Select the significance of 26 November, 1949 in relation to the Constituent Assembly from the following options

options.C: भारत के राष्ट्रीय ध्वज को डिजाइन करना
options.D: संविधान सभा द्वारा संविधान पर हस्ताक्षर

options_english.C: Designing of the National Flag of India
options_english.D: Signing of Constitution by the Constituent Assembly.

questions.solution: On 26th November 1949, the Constitution was adopted and signed by the members of the Constituent Assembly, which is why it is celebrated as Constitution Day.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा जोड़ा सुमेलित है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched ?
questions.solution: In the 1857 revolt, Birjis Qadr was the leader in Lucknow. Other options are incorrect as Kunwar Singh was in Bihar, Nana Saheb in Kanpur, and Gonoo was a tribal leader in Singhbhum.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस शब्द का उपयोग गांधीजी के 'अहिंसा' के दर्शन का वर्णन करने के लिए किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following terms is used to describe Gandhiji's philosophy of 'Non-violence'?
questions.solution: Satyagraha is the term Mahatma Gandhi coined for his philosophy of non-violent resistance and truth, which formed the core of his anti-colonial struggle in India.
questions.chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement

questions.text: नीचे दी गई जानकारी की सहायता से ब्रिटिश अधिकारी की पहचान कीजिए : उन्होंने पश्चिमी शिक्षा की शुरुआत करके भारतीय समाज में सुधार की नीतियाँ अपनाईं । उन्होंने सती प्रथा को ख़त्म करने के लिए कानून बनाए । उन्होंने हिंदू विधवा विवाह को वैधता दी ।
questions.text_english: Identify the name of a British official from the information given below. He adopted policies of reforming Indian society by introducing western education. He established laws to abolish Sati system. He permitted remarriage of Hindu widows
questions.solution: Lord William Bentinck is known for his social reform policies in India, most notably the abolition of the Sati system in 1829 with the help of reformers like Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
questions.chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसकी सलाह पर गांधीजी ने ब्रिटिश भारत में भ्रमण करते हुए भूमि और यहाँ के लोगों के बारे में जानने का प्रयास किया ?
questions.text_english: On whose advice among the following did Gandhiji attempt to visit British India and learn about the land and its people?
questions.solution: Upon returning to India from South Africa, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, whom Gandhiji considered his political mentor, advised him to travel across India to understand the socio-political situation of the country before entering active politics.
questions.chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement

questions.text: (a) पुरातत्वविदों ने हड़प्पा युग के शिल्प उत्पादन केंद्रों की पहचान किस प्रकार की, स्पष्ट कीजिए । अथवा (b) 'हड़प्पा शहरों की सबसे अनूठी विशेषताओं में से एक ध्यानपूर्वक नियोजित जल निकास प्रणाली थी।' इस कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (a) Explain how did archaeologists identify the centres of craft production of the Harappan age. OR (b) The most distinctive feature of Harappan cities was Carefully planned drainage system. Explain the statement.

sub_questions.text: पुरातत्वविदों ने हड़प्पा युग के शिल्प उत्पादन केंद्रों की पहचान किस प्रकार की, स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain how did archaeologists identify the centres of craft production of the Harappan age.

key_points: Archaeologists identify craft production by finding raw materials like stone nodules, shells, and copper ores.
Discovery of tools, unfinished objects, and waste material like heaps of waste or 'debitage' in specific areas.
Presence of kiln structures or specific furnaces used for manufacturing beads or other items in the archaeological remains.

sub_questions.solution: Archaeologists identify Harappan craft production centres primarily through the discovery of archaeological evidence such as raw materials (stone nodules, copper ore, shells), tools used for crafting, and unfinished objects. Most importantly, the presence of heaps of waste material, which is discarded during the production process, serves as a clear indicator that these specific sites were dedicated centres for craft activities.

sub_questions.text: 'हड़प्पा शहरों की सबसे अनूठी विशेषताओं में से एक ध्यानपूर्वक नियोजित जल निकास प्रणाली थी।' इस कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: The most distinctive feature of Harappan cities was Carefully planned drainage system. Explain the statement.

key_points: Systematic planning of streets and drains in a grid-like pattern.
Drains made of baked bricks, covered with slabs, and having manholes for cleaning.
Separation of domestic wastewater from streets via household drainage connections.

sub_questions.solution: The Harappan civilization is renowned for its advanced urban planning. One of its most remarkable features was the drainage system, which was meticulously designed. Streets were laid out in a grid pattern with intersecting drains made of baked bricks. These drains were covered with stone slabs that could be removed for cleaning, and they featured manholes at regular intervals. This indicates that Harappan urban life prioritized hygiene and public sanitation to a high degree.

questions.solution: This is an internal choice question. Students can choose to explain the identification of craft production centres (by analyzing raw materials and production waste) or describe the sophisticated drainage system of the Harappan cities (emphasizing grid layout and sanitation). Both answers require a concise explanation.

questions.text: जैन मान्यता के अनुसार जन्म और पुनर्जन्म का चक्र कर्म के द्वारा निर्धारित होता है।इस कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: According to Jaina teachings, the birth and rebirth is shaped through Karma.Explain the statement.

key_points: Karma in Jainism is a subtle physical substance that adheres to the soul.
Actions, whether physical or mental, accumulate karma based on their nature.
To break the cycle of birth and rebirth, one must practice non-violence and asceticism to clear existing karma and prevent new accumulation.

questions.solution: In Jaina philosophy, karma is considered a subtle material substance that attaches to the soul as a result of an individual's actions, thoughts, and words. These karmic particles weigh down the soul, trapping it in the endless cycle of birth, death, and rebirth (samsara). To achieve liberation, a follower must lead an ascetic life, practice extreme non-violence (ahimsa), and perform penance to purify the soul of its accumulated karmic burden.

questions.text: 1800 ई. में हम्पी के भग्नावशेष कॉलिन मैकेंजी द्वारा प्रकाश में किस प्रकार लाए गए ? विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Analyse how the ruins of Hampi were brought to light in 1800 by Colin Mackenzie.

key_points: Colin Mackenzie was an engineer and antiquarian who worked for the East India Company.
He collected information from local oral traditions and local priests at Virupaksha temple.
He produced the first maps and architectural drawings of Hampi, which helped in its study by later historians.

questions.solution: In 1800, Colonel Colin Mackenzie, an engineer and surveyor with the East India Company, visited Hampi and began the systematic study of its ruins. He relied on information gathered from local oral traditions, specifically from the priests of the Virupaksha temple, to understand the history of the site. His efforts in documentation, including the first maps and detailed architectural drawings of the city, were crucial in bringing the lost history of the Vijayanagara Empire to public attention and academic study.

questions.text: सोलहवीं व सत्रहवीं शताब्दी में ग्रामीण समाज में महिलाओं को एक महत्त्वपूर्ण संसाधन क्यों माना जाता था ? स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain why were women considered an important resource in agrarian society during sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

key_points: Women's labour was essential for agrarian production.
They participated in sowing, weeding, and threshing along with men.
Their roles in specialized work like spinning and textile production provided supplementary family income.

questions.solution: During the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, women were essential to the agrarian economy because their labour was vital in agricultural operations. They worked alongside men in tasks like sowing, weeding, and threshing. Furthermore, women contributed significantly to specialized household crafts such as spinning yarn and weaving, which were crucial for the family's supplementary income. Their participation in both field labour and home production made them integral to the survival and stability of the peasant family.

questions.text: विश्लेषण कीजिए कि उन्नीसवीं सदी की शुरुआत में संथाल लोग राजमहल की पहाड़ियों की परिधि में कैसे बस गए ।
questions.text_english: Analyse how Santhals settled in the periphery of Raj Mahal hills in the beginning of nineteenth century.

key_points: British colonial officials encouraged Santhals to settle in the Damin-i-Koh region.
Santhals were seen as ideal settlers who could clear forests and expand cultivation.
The British wanted to increase land revenue by making the nomadic Santhals sedentary farmers.

questions.solution: In the early nineteenth century, British colonial officials actively encouraged the Santhal people to move into the Raj Mahal hills, specifically the Damin-i-Koh region. The British viewed the Santhals as ideal settlers because they were hardworking and skilled at clearing dense forests, which transformed the land into productive agricultural fields. By settling the Santhals as sedentary farmers, the British aimed to increase tax revenue from the expansion of settled cultivation in areas that were previously underutilized.

questions.text: (a) 1857 के दौरान अफवाहों ने लोगों को अंग्रेजों के खिलाफ विद्रोह करने के लिए किस प्रकार प्रेरित किया ? स्पष्ट कीजिए । अथवा (b) अंग्रेज अवध का अधिग्रहण करने के लिए उत्सुक क्यों थे ? स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (a) How did the rumours play a role in moving the people to revolt against the British during 1857? Explain. OR (b) Why were the British so keen to acquire Awadh? Explain.

sub_questions.text: 1857 के दौरान अफवाहों ने लोगों को अंग्रेजों के खिलाफ विद्रोह करने के लिए किस प्रकार प्रेरित किया ? स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: How did the rumours play a role in moving the people to revolt against the British during 1857? Explain.

key_points: Rumours about greased cartridges triggered fear of religious defilement (Hindu and Muslim).
Reports of bone dust mixed into flour added to the anxiety about social destruction.
These rumours spread rapidly, creating widespread distrust and panic, which unified disparate groups against the British.

sub_questions.solution: During 1857, rumours acted as a powerful catalyst for the rebellion. Reports that the new Enfield rifle cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat deeply offended the religious sentiments of both Hindu and Muslim sepoys, leading them to believe the British were attempting to destroy their caste and religion. Further rumours, such as the claim that bone dust was being mixed into flour to make Indians lose their caste, spread rapidly. This created widespread fear and panic, effectively unifying people across various communities in a common cause to challenge British authority.

sub_questions.text: अंग्रेज अवध का अधिग्रहण करने के लिए उत्सुक क्यों थे ? स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Why were the British so keen to acquire Awadh? Explain.

key_points: Awadh was a very fertile and productive region, highly valuable for its agricultural revenue.
It was strategically located as a buffer and market for British manufactured goods.
The British wanted complete control to implement their land revenue policies effectively.

sub_questions.solution: The British were keen to acquire Awadh because of its immense strategic and economic value. It was a highly fertile region, ideal for growing cotton and indigo, and thus promised high land revenue. Furthermore, the British viewed Awadh as a vital market for their machine-made goods. Lord Dalhousie, who described Awadh as a cherry that would drop into our mouth one day,believed that acquiring it would provide direct control over its resources and ensure it remained under British influence for both economic and political dominance.

questions.solution: This is an internal choice question. Students can choose to write about the impact of rumours on the 1857 revolt (emphasizing religious fear) or the economic and strategic reasons behind the British annexation of Awadh.

questions.text: (a) प्राचीन भारत में राजसत्ता क्षत्रियों के साथ गैर-क्षत्रियों के पास भी होती थी।इस कथन को उदाहरणों सहित स्पष्ट कीजिए । अथवा (b) प्राचीन भारतीय उपमहाद्वीप में चार वर्णों के ब्राह्मणवादी विचार के प्रभाव के परे भी कुछ समुदाय थे।इस कथन को उदाहरणों सहित स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (a) In the ancient India, the Kingship was not only with Kshatriyas but also with Non-Kshatriyas.Explain the statement with examples. OR (b) In the ancient Indian subcontinent there were populations beyond the influence of Brahminical idea of four Varnas.Explain this statement with examples.

key_points: Example of Mauryas (possibly of low origin).
Shungas and Kanvas as Brahmins (not Kshatriyas).
Shakas, Yavanas, and Kushanas (Mlechchhas or foreigners).
Satavahanas as Brahmins.
Forest-dwelling populations.
Nomadic pastoralists.
Groups outside the varna system like Nishadas or Chandalas.

questions.solution: The claim that kingship in ancient India was not limited to Kshatriyas is supported by historical evidence. While the Dharmashastras suggested that only Kshatriyas should be kings, history records different rulers. The Mauryas were often debated to be of low origin. The Shungas and Kanvas were Brahmins, breaking the varna rule. Furthermore, foreign groups like the Shakas, Yavanas, and Kushanas, who were initially considered Mlechchhas (outsiders), became kings and legitimized their rule through patronage of various religions and claiming divine status. Similarly, regarding populations outside the Brahminical four-fold varna system, many groups lived in deep forests, practiced nomadic pastoralism, or existed as tribes like the Nishadas. These groups interacted with the settled society but maintained their distinct cultural and social structures, far removed from the strict varna social norms practiced in the centers of Vedic culture.

questions.text: (a) मुगल भारत के दौरान भूमि के राजकीय स्वामित्व और निजी संपत्ति की कमी के बर्नियर के विवरण की परख कीजिए । अथवा (b) अपनी यात्रा के दौरान दिल्ली और दौलताबाद पर इब्न बतूता के विचारों की परख कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (a) Examine Bernier's description of Crown ownership of land and lack of private property during Mughal India. OR (b) Examine Ibn-Battuta's views on Delhi & Daulatabad during his travel.

key_points: Bernier saw Crown ownership as the cause of India's decline.
He argued that without private property, farmers had no incentive to improve production.
Ibn-Battuta's observations on city planning, infrastructure, and the scale of the two cities.
The description of the market economy, postal systems, and socio-cultural life.

questions.solution: Francois Bernier, a French physician, visited India during the Mughal era and famously critiqued the land system, arguing that the Emperor's absolute ownership of all land prevented the growth of private property. He believed this was a key reason for the relative poverty of Indian peasants and the lack of investment in agricultural improvement, contrasting it negatively with European systems. On the other hand, Ibn-Battuta, a medieval traveller from Morocco, provided a vivid account of the Delhi Sultanate. He described Delhi as a sprawling, populous city with great historical depth and extensive infrastructure. He also noted Daulatabad, its significance, and the way the urban and socio-economic life functioned during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign, highlighting the scale of markets, the postal network, and the architectural grandeur of the region.

questions.text: (a) संविधान सभा के कुछ सदस्यों ने शक्तिशाली केन्द्र के लिए तर्क क्यों दिए ? स्पष्ट कीजिए । अथवा (b) संविधान सभा में कुछ सदस्यों द्वारा निभाई गई महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: (a) Why did some members of Constituent Assembly argue for a strong Centre? Explain. OR (b) Explain the important role played by some members in the Constituent Assembly.

key_points: Arguments for a strong Centre due to post-partition instability and communal tension.
Need for unified national progress and economic planning.
Role of members like Ambedkar, Nehru, Patel, K.M. Munshi, and Alladi Krishnaswamy Aiyar.
Drafting committee contributions and debates on language, minorities, and rights.

questions.solution: During the debates in the Constituent Assembly, several members, including Gopalaswami Ayyangar and K. Santhanam, emphasized the need for a strong central government. This demand was largely driven by the trauma of the Partition of India and the resulting communal violence, which necessitated a centralized authority to maintain national integrity and security. They argued that a powerful Centre was required to plan for economic development effectively and manage national resources. Regarding the role of individual members, stalwarts like Dr. B.R. Ambedkar led the drafting process with meticulous attention to equality and social justice. Jawaharlal Nehru moved the 'Objectives Resolution', setting the ideological framework for the nation. Sardar Patel played a pivotal role in integrating princely states into the Indian Union, while other members engaged in crucial debates regarding fundamental rights, the status of minorities, and the official language, ensuring the constitution addressed the diverse needs of India.

questions.text:
राजन् देवनामपिय पियदस्सी यह कहते हैं :
राजा के आदेश
अतीत में मसलों को निपटाने और नियमित रूप से सूचना एकत्र करने की व्यवस्थाएँ नहीं थीं। लेकिन मैंने निम्नलिखित (व्यवस्था) की हैं। लोगों के समाचार हम तक पतिवेदक सदैव पहुँचाएँ । चाहे मैं कहीं भी हूँ, खाना खा रहा हूँ, अन्तःपुर में हूँ, विश्राम कक्ष में हूँ, गोशाला में हूँ, या फिर पालकी में मुझे ले जाया जा रहा हो अथवा वाटिका में हूँ। मैं लोगों के विषयों का निराकरण हर स्थल पर करूँगा ।
questions.text_english:
The orders of the king
Thus speaks king Devanampiya Piyadassi :
In the past, there were no arrangements for disposing affairs, nor for receiving regular reports.
But I have made the following (arrangement). Pativedakas should report to me about the affairs of the people at all times, anywhere, whether I am eating, in the inner apartment, in the bedroom, in the cow pen, being carried (possibly in a palanquin), or in the garden.
And I will dispose of the affairs of the people everywhere.

sub_questions.text: देवनामपिय पियदस्सी किसे कहा गया है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Who was referred to as Devanampiya Piyadassi?

key_points: King Ashoka.

sub_questions.solution: Devanampiya Piyadassi refers to the Mauryan Emperor Ashoka.

sub_questions.text: देवनामपिय का दृष्टिकोण पूर्व के प्रकरण के निपटान की व्यवस्थाओं की तुलना में किस प्रकार अलग था ?
sub_questions.text_english: How did Devanampiya's approach differ from past arrangements regarding the handling of affairs?

key_points: Unlike the past, he introduced a regular system to receive reports.
He ensured he was accessible to receive information at all times.

sub_questions.solution: Unlike the past, when there was no formal arrangement for receiving regular reports on public affairs, Ashoka established a system where his reporters (Pativedakas) could inform him about public matters at any time and location.

sub_questions.text: देवनामपिय ने किस तरह से सूचना प्राप्त की और लोगों के मसलों को निपटाया ?
sub_questions.text_english: In what way did Devanampiya receive reports and disposed of the affairs of the people?

key_points: He received reports through Pativedakas (reporters).
He made himself accessible everywhere, ensuring he could attend to matters even during private activities.

sub_questions.solution: Ashoka received information through his specially appointed reporters known as Pativedakas. He ensured that these reporters could reach him regardless of his activities—whether he was dining, resting, or in his private quarters—demonstrating his commitment to being accessible to the people and disposing of their affairs personally wherever he was.

questions.solution: The passage details Ashoka's innovative administrative efforts to remain informed and responsive to his subjects' needs, demonstrating a departure from past administrative inactivity.

questions.text:
यह रचना कबीर की मानी जाती है :
एक ईश्वर
हे भाई यह बताओ, किस तरह हो सकता है
कि संसार के एक नहीं दो स्वामी हों ?
किसने तुम्हें भ्रमित किया है ?
ईश्वर को अनेक नामों से पुकारा जाता है: जैसे अल्लाह, राम, करीम, केशव, हरि तथा हज़रत ।
विभिन्नताएँ तो केवल शब्दों में हैं जिनका आविष्कार हम स्वयं करते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Here is a composition attributed to Kabir:
The One Lord
Tell me, brother, how can there be
No one lord of the world but two?
Who led you so astray?
God is called by many names:
Names like Allah, Ram, Karim, Keshav, Hari, and Hazrat.
Gold may be shaped into rings and bangles.
Isn't it gold all the same?
Distinctions are only words we invent...

sub_questions.text: कबीर ने परम सत्यता का विवरण कैसे किया है ?
sub_questions.text_english: How did Kabir describe the ultimate reality?

key_points: Ultimate reality is one (Monotheistic).
Differences in names are human inventions.

sub_questions.solution: Kabir describes the ultimate reality as singular. He asserts that while God is called by various names like Allah, Ram, or Hari, these distinctions are merely words invented by humans to confuse themselves.

sub_questions.text: कबीर का दर्शन अध्यात्म की व्यापक समझ में कैसे योगदान देता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: How does Kabir's philosophy contribute to a broader understanding of spiritualism?

key_points: It promotes unity beyond sectarian divides.
It highlights the essence of divinity over ritualistic naming.

sub_questions.solution: Kabir's philosophy contributes to a broader understanding of spiritualism by advocating for unity and transcending sectarian divisions. He shifts the focus from rituals and external labels to the core essence of the divine, promoting a universal spiritual vision.

sub_questions.text: कबीर ने किस प्रकार मानवता के प्रति समावेशी और दयालु दृष्टिकोण की बात की है ?
sub_questions.text_english: How has Kabir advocated an inclusive and compassionate view of humanity?

key_points: By ignoring religious boundaries.
Comparing different religions to forms of gold, emphasizing underlying unity.
Rejecting artificial distinctions to foster human brotherhood.

sub_questions.solution: Kabir advocates for an inclusive and compassionate view of humanity by ignoring the rigid boundaries of religious sects. He uses the metaphor of gold—which remains the same regardless of whether it is fashioned into a ring or a bangle—to explain that beneath diverse religious forms, the essence of humanity and the divine remains identical. By rejecting artificial distinctions, he fosters a sense of brotherhood and empathy.

questions.solution: This passage highlights Kabir's Nirguna Bhakti philosophy, emphasizing the unity of God and critiquing the superficial divisions maintained by organized religion.

questions.text:
चरखा
महात्मा गाँधी आधुनिक युग, जिसमें मशीनों ने मानव को गुलाम बनाकर श्रम को हटा दिया था, के घोर आलोचक थे । उन्होंने चरखा को एक ऐसे, मानव समाज के प्रतीक रूप में देखा, जिसमें मशीनों और प्रौद्योगिकी को बहुत महिमामंडित नहीं किया जाएगा। इससे भी अधिक चरखा गरीबों को पूरक आमदनी प्रदान कर सकता था तथा उन्हें स्वावलम्बी बना सकता था ।

'यंग इंडिया, 13 नवंबर 1924'
खद्दर मशीनरी को नष्ट नहीं करना चाहता बल्कि यह इसके प्रयोग को नियमित करता है और इसके विकास को नियंत्रित करता है। यह मशीनरी का प्रयोग सर्वाधिक ग़रीब लोगों के लिए उनकी अपनी झोपड़ियों में करता है। पहिया अपने आप में ही मशीनरी का एक उत्कृष्ट नमूना है।
'यंग इंडिया, 17 मार्च 1927'
questions.text_english:
Charkha
Mahatma Gandhi was profoundly critical of the modern age in which machines enslaved humans and displaced labour. He saw the charkha as a symbol of a human society that would not glorify machines and technology. The spinning wheel, moreover, could provide the poor with supplementary income and make them self-reliant.

'YOUNG INDIA, 13 NOVEMBER 1924'
Khaddar does not seek to destroy all machinery but it does regulate its use and check its weedy growth. It uses machinery for the service of the poorest in their own cottages. The wheel is itself an exquisite piece of machinery.
'YOUNG INDIA, 17 MARCH 1927'

sub_questions.text: गांधीजी मशीन के आलोचक क्यों थे ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why was Gandhiji critical of machines?

key_points: They displaced labor.
They enslaved humans.
They led to unemployment.

sub_questions.solution: Gandhiji was critical of modern machinery because he believed it enslaved humans and displaced manual labor, leading to unemployment and misery for the poorest segments of society.

sub_questions.text: पहिये को मशीनरी का एक उत्कृष्ट नमूना क्यों माना गया था ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why was wheel considered as an exquisite piece of machinery?

key_points: It is simple and efficient.
It enables production at the cottage level without exploitation.

sub_questions.solution: The spinning wheel was considered an exquisite piece of machinery because it was simple, efficient, and could serve the poorest people within their own homes, promoting self-reliance rather than exploitation.

sub_questions.text: गांधीजी ने चरखे को कैसे महिमामंडित किया है ?

key_points: As a symbol of human society that doesn't glorify industrial technology.
As a tool for self-reliance and extra income for the poor.
As a way to regulate and service the poor.

sub_questions.solution: Gandhiji glorified the charkha by presenting it as a powerful symbol of a human-centric society that resisted the worship of industrial technology. He emphasized that it provided the poor with supplementary income, fostered self-reliance, and represented a balanced use of machinery that served the most marginalized individuals in their own cottages.

questions.solution: This passage reflects Gandhi's economic philosophy, which focused on cottage industries, self-sufficiency, and resistance to dehumanizing industrialization.
questions.chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement

questions.text: 34.1 भारत के दिए गए राजनीतिक रेखा-मानचित्र में निम्नलिखित को उपयुक्त चिह्नों से अंकित कीजिए और उनके नाम लिखिए : (i) अमरावती (बौद्ध स्थल), (ii) वाराणसी (प्राचीन नगर), (iii) (a) विजयनगर (14वीं सदी का एक साम्राज्य) अथवा (b) उड़ीसा (14वीं सदी का क्षेत्र) 34.2 भारत के इसी राजनीतिक रेखा-मानचित्र पर दो स्थानों को A और B, 1857 के विद्रोह के केन्द्रों में चिह्नित किया गया है। इनको पहचानिए और उनके सही नाम उनके निकट खींची गई रेखाओं पर लिखिए ।
questions.text_english: 34.1 On the given political outline map of India, locate and label the following with appropriate signs: (i) Amravati (Buddhist site), (ii) Varanasi (Ancient city), (iii) (a) Vijayanagara (An Empire of 14th century) OR (b) Orissa (Territory of 14th century) 34.2 On the same political outline map of India two places related with the centres of revolt of 1857 one marked as A and B. Identify them and write their names on the lines marked near them.
questions.instruction_line: Note: For Visually Impaired candidates, there are alternative questions provided in the paper.
questions.instruction_line_english: Note: For Visually Impaired candidates, there are alternative questions provided in the paper.

key_points: Amravati marked in Andhra Pradesh.
Varanasi marked in Uttar Pradesh.
Vijayanagara marked in Karnataka.
A (1857 revolt) is Delhi.
B (1857 revolt) is Lucknow/Awadh region.

questions.solution: This is a map-based question. Students are expected to plot the historical locations on an outline map of India. 34.1 involves locating Amravati (Andhra Pradesh), Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh), and Vijayanagara (Karnataka). 34.2 requires identifying A as Delhi and B as Lucknow, which were key centres of the 1857 uprising.
